compiled_state.title: As an operator, the outbound bridge processes every event between cron ticks via a SHA-based checkpoint cursor with bounded fetch and per-event partial-success advance
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Replace the HEAD~1..HEAD diff window in the outbound bridge with a SHA-based checkpoint cursor stored on the tracker branch. Bound fetch depth, cap commit windows, advance per-event on partial Jira push success, define cold-start/corruption/unreachable-SHA recovery, add a workflow concurrency group.

**Why**: This is the PRIMARY chronic root cause. Empirically confirmed at run 25501576353: HEAD~1..HEAD returned only suggestion files; cluster STATUS events at HEAD~4..HEAD~6 invisible. Every cron tick where two or more commits land between ticks silently drops events older than HEAD.

**Scope**:
- IN: bridge-outbound.py cursor logic, outbound-bridge.yml fetch depth + concurrency group, .outbound-checkpoint.json persistence (atomic via existing _atomic_write_json), per-event checkpoint advance on partial success, cold-start/corruption/unreachable-SHA/ahead-of-HEAD all seed at HEAD with BRIDGE_ALERT, 500-commit cap with BRIDGE_ALERT.
- OUT: BRIDGE_ENV_ID hygiene (S2), ADF parsing (S3), user-map (S4), regression test suite (S5), webhook-based real-time dispatch (out of epic).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, three back-to-back local STATUS commits authored across one cron interval all reach Jira within the next outbound run — verified by a fixture replay test that creates 3 commits older than HEAD~1 and asserts all 3 are observed by process_events ← Satisfies: "The outbound bridge processes every event added to the tracker between cron ticks, including events older than HEAD~1, without replaying full history on cold-start"
- When this story is complete, on cold-start (no .outbound-checkpoint.json present), the cursor seeds at HEAD, emits a one-shot BRIDGE_ALERT, and does NOT push any prior history to Jira — verified by a fixture test that runs the bridge with no checkpoint file and asserts zero Jira pushes plus a BRIDGE_ALERT ← Satisfies: same SC (cold-start clause)
- When this story is complete, on checkpoint corruption, malformed-JSON, unreachable-SHA, or checkpoint-ahead-of-HEAD, the cursor falls back to seed-at-HEAD with BRIDGE_ALERT — covered by 4 unit tests, one per recovery case ← Satisfies: same SC
- When this story is complete, partial Jira push success advances the checkpoint to the SHA of the highest successfully-pushed event (not stays at prior, not jumps to HEAD) — verified by a fixture where event N+1 fails and the next run resumes from event N+2 with no duplicate of event N ← Satisfies: same SC
- When this story is complete, fetch uses --deepen=50 first and only escalates to --unshallow when the checkpoint SHA is unreachable; the commit window is hard-capped at 500 commits and exceeding the cap triggers seed-at-HEAD with BRIDGE_ALERT ← Satisfies: same SC
- When this story is complete, the outbound workflow declares concurrency group bridge-outbound with cancel-in-progress false, preventing cron + workflow_dispatch + inbound from racing on the checkpoint write ← Satisfies: same SC
- When this story is complete, unit tests cover process_events with a multi-commit fixture (3+ commits) and confirm all events are returned, not just the most recent commit's events ← Satisfies: TDD DoD for code-change story (unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic)

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Atomic checkpoint write must use the existing bridge._atomic.atomic_write_json pattern — do NOT introduce a parallel atomicity primitive.
- [Performance] The 500-commit cap is a safety valve for thundering-herd on Jira recovery from a multi-day stall; document the cap and the BRIDGE_ALERT path in the cursor module docstring.
- [Testing] At least one test must drive the actual workflow entry-point script (not the Python module directly) so shell-level diff-window regressions are caught — the original HEAD~1..HEAD bug lived in shell, not Python.
- [Maintainability] The checkpoint file format must mirror the inbound checkpoint shape: {"last_processed_sha": "...", "last_run_id": "..."} written via _atomic_write_json before the workflow's commit step (matching bridge-inbound.py:154-176 lifecycle).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
